The main takeaway from our work is that
, in large markets, there is a single allocation mechanism that satisfies efficiency, symmetry, and strategy-proofness.
the choice of mechanism for allocating resources in environments with no transfers may be less critical for the resulting allocations than previously thought, at least in large markets.
the design of large markets can focus on efficiency and fairness, rather than incentives, as these goals can be achieved without sacrificing the other.
